# TABLES — kind against outcome, over the committed record

Roots read: **55** of 55 attempted. Artifacts: **6789**.

## The operationalization

`Artifact` carries no kind field. Formal-vs-informal is a fact about `Interface.commitments`, read three ways — exactly the three the code itself reads:

| reading | test | what in the code reads it |
|---|---|---|
| **K1 battery-carrying** | ≥1 registered commitment with `programs.evaluable` true | `coverage` (the Pareto axis), `_evaluable_battery`, `crit_program` |
| **K2 substantive-backed** | ≥1 registered SUBSTANTIVE commitment (`measures/reach._substantive` — evaluable and not structural well-formedness) | `formally_backed`, the prose-immunity guard |
| **K3 execution-backed** | ≥1 commitment in `oracle.EXEC_PROGRAMS` | `execution_backed`, `_standing_recrit_pool` |

K3 ⊆ K2 ⊆ K1. "Prose" in each table means NOT formal by that reading.

CONTENT FORM (does the artifact's own text parse as an envelope or a skeleton) is reported separately below and is never substituted for the three above: it is what a reader would call formal-looking, and it is not what any guard consults.

### Content form against K1 — the two do not line up

| content form | battery-carrying | not |
|---|---|---|
| free-prose | 709 | 4048 |
| json-other | 15 | 330 |
| skeleton | 1687 | 0 |

This cross-tab is the reason the tables below use the commitment readings and not the text's appearance.
